title: Agents and tool execution
summary: Turn model suggestions into controlled actions.
detail: An agent combines a model, state, tools and an execution loop. Make the boundary between a proposed action and an authorized effect visible. Evaluate the resulting state, not only the final message.
failures: A persuasive final answer can conceal a failed action.

title: Operations and evidence
summary: Keep the service understandable when it succeeds or fails.
detail: Separate operational health from answer quality. Correlate requests, model calls and tool outcomes, then link failures to reproducible evaluation cases. Define retention and access for the evidence itself.
failures: A green uptime dashboard can coexist with wrong answers.

title: Model hosting and capacity
summary: Choose where inference runs and test the resource budget.
detail: Compare provider APIs with a model server you operate. Evaluate the intended context lengths and concurrency on the actual hardware. Cloud deployment, local inference and on-premises operation are distinct choices.
failures: A model that loads can still fail under concurrent long contexts.

title: Adaptation and learning
summary: Improve behavior using examples and an explicit objective.
detail: Prompt optimization changes instructions or demonstrations. Fine-tuning changes model weights. Both need independent evaluation, data provenance and a baseline that justifies the extra complexity.
failures: Optimizing the test set makes the reported improvement unreliable.

sources.title: Joint prompt and weight optimization paper

title: Tool-calling loop
summary: Let the model request a tool, then return its result.
detail: The application owns argument validation, authorization, execution and stopping conditions. Feed typed results or explicit errors back into the next model step. Bound steps, duration and spend; a tool request is not permission.
failures: Repeated calls exhaust the budget.
A failed tool is described as successful.

title: Tool contracts
summary: Specify what a tool accepts, returns and changes.
detail: A useful contract describes the input schema, result schema, error states and side effects. Server validation must also check resource ownership. A syntactically valid resource ID may refer to someone else’s data.
failures: Schema-valid arguments target an unauthorized resource.
An empty result conceals a tool error.

title: ACP: Agent Client Protocol
summary: Connect a user interface to an agent session.
detail: ACP defines session prompts, streamed updates, capability negotiation and cancellation. Optional capabilities determine available behavior such as session loading. It connects a client to an agent, not directly to interchangeable model weights.
failures: Assuming every backend supports resume.
Treating a reported tool event as proof of safe execution.

title: MCP: Model Context Protocol
summary: Connect an application to tools, resources and prompts.
detail: An MCP host manages clients connected to servers. Capability discovery and tool invocation standardize a seam; the host still decides how context reaches the model and when an action is permitted.
failures: Server content contains malicious instructions.
Tool discovery is mistaken for authorization.

title: CHAP: Collaborative Human-Agent Protocol
summary: Record structured work, reviews and decisions between participants.
detail: CHAP coordinates task state and review decisions. Profiles add capabilities; deployments must verify actual enforcement. Evidence-chain consistency does not prove complete records or factual artifacts. Mako’s example maps ACP permissions to core, review and control interactions.
failures: A recorded approval can concern a factually wrong artifact.
Advertising a profile is mistaken for verified enforcement.

title: Authorization at execution
summary: Check whether this caller may perform this action now.
detail: Enforce scope and resource ownership at the tool boundary. A model choice, UI confirmation or tool description must not substitute for server authorization. Tests should attempt forbidden actions and verify that no effect occurs.
failures: The model supplies a more privileged account ID.
Approval applies to different arguments than the execution.

title: Bounded retries
summary: Retry transient failures without repeating harmful effects.
detail: Classify errors before retrying. Cap attempts and use backoff. A timeout can occur after a remote write succeeded, so the next attempt needs an idempotent operation or an outcome check.
failures: Blind retries create duplicate writes.
Nested retry policies multiply load.

title: Idempotent actions
summary: Make a repeated request represent the same intended action.
detail: Use a caller-supplied operation identity and store the accepted result at the effect boundary. Bind that identity to the request meaning. Reusing a key with changed arguments must not silently replay an unrelated result.
failures: A fresh key on each retry creates duplicates.
Deduplication state expires before a delayed retry.

title: Cancellation and stale results
summary: Stop further work and explain what already happened.
detail: Propagate cancellation through the session and pending permission requests. Reject late approvals for cancelled work. Cancellation does not undo an external effect that already completed; report that outcome separately.
failures: A late approval restarts cancelled work.
The UI claims a completed external action was undone.

sources.title: ACP tool calls and permission requests

title: Prompt injection
summary: Untrusted content can try to redirect the agent.
detail: Treat retrieved text, web pages and tool results as data. Keep credentials and authority outside model-produced arguments. Exercise malicious fixtures through the whole tool path; a prompt-only warning cannot enforce access boundaries.
failures: A document instructs the agent to disclose secrets.
A tool result impersonates a trusted instruction.

title: LangChain and LangGraph
summary: Compose model and tool steps with explicit workflow state.
detail: LangChain provides model, tool and agent abstractions. LangGraph supplies lower-level stateful orchestration, persistence and interrupts. Evaluate whether a plain function workflow is sufficient before adding graph state and checkpoint maintenance.
failures: A replay repeats an external side effect.
Persistent state and deployed code no longer agree.

title: LlamaIndex
summary: Connect data retrieval and agent workflows.
detail: LlamaIndex provides ingestion, retrieval, query and agent components. Keep document IDs and retrieval evidence visible through abstractions so a failed answer can be traced back to the selected passages.
failures: A convenient integration hides source provenance.
Changing the retriever silently changes answer support.

title: Request and agent traces
summary: Follow one request across retrieval, models and tools.
detail: Use related spans to locate latency and failures. Record configuration IDs, safe document references and error categories. Treat prompt text and tool arguments as sensitive data; recording every value is not required for useful diagnostics.
failures: Traces expose private content.
Missing spans make the apparent path incomplete.

title: OpenTelemetry
summary: Collect telemetry with shared instrumentation interfaces.
detail: OpenTelemetry supplies APIs, SDKs and signal conventions. An exporter sends selected telemetry to a chosen destination. It is not a storage backend or a quality evaluator; configure collection and access deliberately.
failures: Exporter settings send content to an unintended destination.
Sampling omits a rare failure.

code.text:
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
tracer = provider.get_tracer("map.example")
with tracer.start_as_current_span("retrieve") as span:
    span.set_attribute("example.result_count", 2)
finished, = exporter.get_finished_spans()
assert dict(finished.attributes) == {"example.result_count": 2}
provider.shutdown()

title: Monitoring and alerts
summary: Detect user-visible degradation across many requests.
detail: Track latency distributions, error rates and load. Add separately measured quality signals for AI behavior. Alert on actionable symptoms with an owner and response path rather than every noisy metric.
failures: Average latency conceals slow tails.
Telemetry success is mistaken for answer correctness.

title: Service objectives and error budgets
summary: Define how much failure the service can tolerate.
detail: Specify eligible requests, what counts as good, the target and the measurement window. Pair availability and latency objectives with separate quality evaluation. An SLO is an engineering target; an SLA adds contractual consequences.
failures: The denominator excludes affected users.
An uptime target is presented as a factual-accuracy promise.

title: Incident response
summary: Contain harm, restore service and preserve evidence.
detail: Assign an incident lead, record decisions and separate mitigation from investigation. For AI incidents, capture the affected model, prompt, corpus and tool policy versions without copying private content into unrestricted channels.
failures: Responders change multiple variables without a record.
Sensitive examples are copied into broad logs.

title: Release and rollback
summary: Restore a known working configuration after a regression.
detail: Release a versioned bundle and check a limited rollout before wider traffic. Preserve the prior model, prompt, index and tool contracts. Reverting code cannot automatically reverse external writes already performed.
failures: The old index cannot be reconstructed.
Rollback is confused with undoing external effects.

title: Langfuse
summary: Inspect traces and connect examples to evaluation.
detail: Langfuse combines LLM observability, prompt management and evaluation workflows. Use it to investigate individual failures and compare runs; reviewed labels and evaluator calibration remain the team’s responsibility.
failures: Trace capture contains personal data.
A score is accepted without examining the rubric.

title: MLflow
summary: Track AI experiments, traces and evaluation results.
detail: Record the configuration and artifacts behind each run so candidate behavior can be compared and reproduced. MLflow supplies tracking and evaluation tooling, not a task-independent definition of a correct answer.
failures: Two scores refer to different datasets.
An artifact version is missing from the result.

title: Evaluation frameworks
summary: Automate checks while retaining control of the question being measured.
detail: Ragas supports evaluation workflows; DeepEval offers test-oriented evaluation; promptfoo compares prompts and runs assertions; TruLens links traces and feedback. Choose by the required metric, data path and reproducibility, not by a single headline score.
failures: A judge rewards fluent unsupported text.
Different tool defaults make scores incomparable.

title: vLLM
summary: Serve supported models with an optimized inference engine.
detail: vLLM manages inference execution, scheduling and memory for supported configurations. Benchmark the chosen model and hardware with realistic input and output lengths. An API-compatible endpoint still needs deployment authentication and capacity controls.
failures: A supported model exceeds memory at target concurrency.
Throughput improves while user latency worsens.

title: llama.cpp
summary: Run compatible models across local hardware options.
detail: llama.cpp provides inference and server tooling with quantized model support. Choose a compatible artifact and backend, then test quality and speed on the actual machine. A local endpoint is not automatically private if exposed on the network.
failures: The model format or backend is incompatible.
A bound network interface exposes the endpoint.

title: Ollama
summary: Manage models and call an inference API.
detail: Ollama exposes model APIs and local model management. Make the server destination and model identity explicit. A client library can target another host, so local installation alone does not establish where each request runs.
failures: An environment setting targets an unintended server.
A model tag changes without a recorded revision.

title: Inference capacity
summary: Measure how many requests fit within latency and memory limits.
detail: Test context length, output length, concurrency and workload mix together. Separate time to first token from later token speed. Weight size is only part of memory use; caches and runtime buffers also consume capacity.
failures: A short-prompt benchmark hides long-context failures.
A weight-only estimate ignores runtime memory.
formula: ideal_weight_bytes = parameter_count × bits_per_weight / 8; total_memory > weight_bytes in a running server

code.text:
parameters = 8_000_000_000
bits_per_weight = 4
ideal_weight_bytes = parameters * bits_per_weight // 8
print(ideal_weight_bytes / 1_000_000_000, 'GB of ideal weights only')
assert ideal_weight_bytes == 4_000_000_000

title: Quantization
summary: Use lower-precision representations to reduce resource needs.
detail: A lower-precision artifact can reduce weight memory and may improve speed on supported hardware. Measure task quality after conversion. Precision labels alone do not determine accuracy, runtime support or end-to-end memory use.
failures: A rare task regresses despite average score stability.
The hardware lacks an efficient kernel for the format.

title: DSPy
summary: Optimize a language-model program against an explicit metric.
detail: DSPy expresses programs as modules and offers optimizers for instructions, demonstrations and supported weight-training paths. The program, examples and metric define the objective. Keep final evaluation cases outside optimization.
failures: The optimizer exploits a weak metric.
Evaluation examples leak into demonstrations.

title: Prompt optimization
summary: Search for instructions and examples that improve task results.
detail: Optimize prompt instructions or demonstrations while keeping model weights fixed. DSPy MIPROv2 is one implementation. Compare the result on untouched cases and record the search budget; an improved training score alone is insufficient.
failures: The prompt memorizes examples.
The objective favors verbosity over usefulness.

code.text:
import dspy

# Supply your configured program, metric and separate data splits.
optimizer = dspy.MIPROv2(metric=task_metric)
candidate = optimizer.compile(program, trainset=train_cases)
# Evaluate candidate on untouched test_cases before release.

title: Supervised fine-tuning
summary: Train model behavior from input and desired-output examples.
detail: SFT updates trainable weights to reduce a training objective on examples. The dataset format and loss masking determine which tokens teach the model. Check task gains and regressions against the original model on held-out data.
failures: Train and test cases overlap.
The model learns incorrect or private target text.

title: PEFT
summary: Adapt a model while training a subset of parameters.
detail: The PEFT library implements parameter-efficient methods and adapter workflows. It can reduce the training and storage burden compared with full fine-tuning. Runtime compatibility and task quality still need validation.
failures: The adapter is paired with a different base revision.
A smaller trainable set fails to learn the target behavior.

title: LoRA adapters
summary: Learn a low-rank update to selected model weights.
detail: LoRA represents an update through smaller matrices while the base weights can remain frozen. Rank controls adaptation capacity and parameter count. Store the base revision with the adapter and evaluate their combination.
failures: A low rank cannot express the required change.
An adapter is loaded onto an incompatible base model.
formula: W′ = W + ΔW; ΔW = B A, where rank(ΔW) ≤ r

title: Training data and splits
summary: Choose examples that represent the intended behavior.
detail: Record provenance, permissions, labels and split membership. Separate related documents or conversations before splitting so near-duplicates do not leak into evaluation. Preserve unknown labels as unknown rather than inventing negatives.
outputs: Versioned train, validation and test sets
failures: Near-duplicates inflate apparent performance.
Missing labels become false negative labels.

title: Synthetic training examples
summary: Generate candidate examples, then review their quality and coverage.
detail: Synthetic examples can expand scenarios and formats. Retain generator and seed-source provenance, verify labels and check duplicates against held-out cases. A generator’s confidence is not independent evidence that its answer is correct.
failures: The generator repeats the base model’s mistakes.
Synthetic examples contaminate the final evaluation.

title: Version the complete system
summary: Record enough configuration to explain and reproduce a result.
detail: Track model revision, tokenizer, prompt, code, dataset, index, adapter and evaluator versions as applicable. A model name alone does not identify the system. Reproduction also depends on runtime and nondeterministic behavior.
failures: A mutable model tag changes between runs.
The index or evaluator version is absent.

title: Haystack
summary: Build search and agent workflows from reusable components.
detail: Haystack connects document stores, retrievers, generators and tools through pipelines. Keep each component’s contract and evaluation visible. A pipeline that executes successfully can still select irrelevant evidence or generate an unsupported answer.
failures: A component upgrade changes result meaning.
Pipeline success is mistaken for answer correctness.
